title: C# Course Overview
learningObjectives: Describe the scope and sequence of this C# course.
Distinguish C# from the .NET runtime, SDK and libraries.
Identify major application areas supported by .NET.
Recognize the course's example, practice and validation standards.

understand.concept: C# is a strongly typed, general-purpose programming language in the .NET ecosystem. This course begins with language foundations and the tools used to build and run programs, then develops control flow, methods, object-oriented design, collections, error handling, files, LINQ, asynchronous programming and professional application practices.
understand.whyItMatters: A clear course map helps learners connect syntax lessons to the larger work of building maintainable applications and avoids confusing a language with a framework or editor.
understand.analogy: Think of C# as the language used to describe a program, the .NET runtime as the environment that executes it, and the SDK as the workbench for creating, building and testing it.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies a real toolchain. The compiler, runtime, libraries, build system and operating system have distinct responsibilities and compatibility rules.

explain.narrative:
## The learning path

The course starts with C#, the .NET SDK and console programs. It then covers values and types, expressions, decisions, loops, arrays and methods. Later modules teach classes, interfaces, records, generics, collections, exceptions, file I/O, delegates, events, LINQ, asynchronous programming and application engineering.

## Language, platform and tools

C# defines source-language syntax and semantics. .NET provides a runtime, base libraries and application infrastructure. The .NET SDK includes command-line tools such as `dotnet` for creating, building, testing and publishing projects. An editor is a development aid, not the language runtime.

## Validation policy

Examples use a dedicated .NET SDK workflow, not the HTML/CSS/JavaScript playground. The initial reproducible baseline is .NET 10 LTS with its default C# 14 language version. Each lesson remains draft until structural, compilation, execution, assessment and editorial checks are evidenced.
